questions.question: In the namespace `storage-task`, create a PVC `data-pvc` (StorageClass `standard`, `ReadWriteOnce`, `2Gi`) and a Pod `data-pod` (image `nginx`) that mounts it as the volume `data` at `/usr/share/nginx/html`. The Pod must be Running.

verification.description: PVC exists with correct specifications
Pod exists and is running
PVC is correctly mounted in the pod

questions.question: Create a StorageClass `fast-local` with the provisioner `rancher.io/local-path` and `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer`, and make it the **only** default StorageClass of the cluster.

verification.description: StorageClass exists with correct specifications
StorageClass is set as default
No other StorageClass is marked as default

questions.question:
Create a PersistentVolume `manual-pv` (`1Gi`, `ReadWriteOnce`, hostPath `/mnt/data`) that can only be used on the node `k3d-cluster-agent-0` (node affinity on `kubernetes.io/hostname`).

In the namespace `manual-storage`, create a PVC `manual-pvc` (`1Gi`, `ReadWriteOnce`) that is Bound to `manual-pv`, and a Pod `manual-pod` (image `busybox`, `command: ["sleep", "3600"]`) that mounts it at `/data`.

verification.description: PV exists with correct specifications
PVC exists and is bound to PV
Pod exists, is running, and uses the PVC

questions.question: In the namespace `scaling`, create a Deployment `scaling-app` (image `nginx`, `2` replicas, Pod label `app=scaling-app`) with requests `cpu: 200m`, `memory: 256Mi` and limits `cpu: 500m`, `memory: 512Mi`. Autoscale it with an `autoscaling/v1` HorizontalPodAutoscaler named `scaling-app`: `2` to `5` replicas at `70%` CPU.

verification.description: Deployment exists with correct specifications
HPA exists with correct specifications
Deployment has correct resource configurations

questions.question:
Label the node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` with `disk=ssd`. In the namespace `scheduling`, create a Deployment `app-scheduling` (`3` replicas, image `nginx`) that can only run on nodes labeled `disk=ssd`, using `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` node affinity with the expression `disk In (ssd)` (not a `nodeSelector`). All Pods must run on `k3d-cluster-agent-1`.

Do this before Question 7, which taints that node.

verification.description: Node is correctly labeled
Deployment exists with correct node affinity
All pods are running on the correct node

questions.question:
Label the existing namespace `security` with `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted` and `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce-version=latest`. Then run a Pod `secure-pod` there with the image `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27` that the `restricted` policy accepts:

- Pod security context: `runAsUser: 1000`, `runAsNonRoot: true`, `seccompProfile.type: RuntimeDefault`
- Container security context: `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `runAsUser: 1000`, drop `ALL` capabilities
- An `emptyDir` volume `html` mounted at `/usr/share/nginx/html`

verification.description: Pod Security Policy exists with correct specifications
Pod exists and complies with the policy

questions.question:
Taint the node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` with `special-workload=true:NoSchedule`. In the namespace `scheduling`, create two Deployments with `2` replicas of `nginx` each:

- `toleration-deploy`, which tolerates exactly this taint (operator `Equal`, value `true`, effect `NoSchedule`)
- `normal-deploy`, without any toleration

All Pods of both Deployments must be Running.

verification.description: Node is correctly tainted
Toleration deployment exists and pods are scheduled correctly
Normal deployment exists and pods avoid tainted node

questions.question: In the namespace `stateful`, create a StatefulSet `web` (`3` replicas, image `nginx`, Pod label `app=web`) whose `serviceName` is the headless Service `web-svc` (selector `app=web`, port `80`). Each Pod gets its own volume from a `volumeClaimTemplate` named `www` (`1Gi`, `ReadWriteOnce`, StorageClass `cold`) mounted at `/usr/share/nginx/html`. The PVCs `www-web-0` to `www-web-2` must be Bound.

verification.description: StatefulSet exists with correct specifications
Headless service exists and is configured correctly
PVCs are created and bound correctly

questions.question:
In the namespace `dns-debug`:

- Deployment `web-app`: `3` replicas, image `nginx`, Pod label `app=web-app`, exposed by a ClusterIP Service `web-svc` on port `80`
- ConfigMap `dns-config` that stores your custom search domains (for example the key `searches` with `dns-debug.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local`)
- Pod `dns-test` (image `busybox`) running `wget -qO- http://web-svc && wget -qO- http://web-svc.dns-debug.svc.cluster.local && sleep 36000`, with `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst` and the same search domains in `spec.dnsConfig.searches`

verification.description: Deployment and service exist and are correctly configured
DNS test pod exists and can resolve service
DNS configuration is correct with custom search domains

questions.question: In the namespace `dns-config`, create a Deployment `dns-app` (`2` replicas, image `nginx`) exposed by a Service `dns-svc` on port `80`. Then run a Pod `dns-tester` (image `infoblox/dnstools`) that writes the `nslookup` output for both `dns-svc` and `dns-svc.dns-config.svc.cluster.local` to `/tmp/dns-test.txt` inside the Pod, and keeps running afterwards.

verification.description: Deployment and service exist and are correctly configured
DNS resolution works correctly
Test results are properly stored

- `overlays/production/kustomization.yaml`: based on `../../base`, with the namespace `kustomize`, the label `environment=production` on the Deployment and its Pods, `3` replicas, and a ConfigMap `nginx-config` with `index.html=Welcome to Production` (a generator is fine) mounted in the nginx container as the volume `nginx-index` at `/usr/share/nginx/html`

questions.question:
In the namespace `gateway` (the Gateway API CRDs and the GatewayClass `ckx-gateway` are installed; there is no controller, so only the resources are graded):

- a Gateway `main-gateway` with the class `ckx-gateway` and one listener `http`, protocol `HTTP`, port `80`
- Deployments `app1` and `app2` (image `nginx`) with Services `app1-svc` and `app2-svc` on port `8080` (target port `80`)
- an HTTPRoute attached to `main-gateway` that sends `PathPrefix /app1` to `app1-svc:8080` and `PathPrefix /app2` to `app2-svc:8080`

verification.description: Gateway resource exists and is configured correctly
HTTPRoute exists with correct routing rules
Backend services and deployments are running

questions.question:
In the namespace `limits`:

- a LimitRange of type `Container`: default request `cpu: 100m`, `memory: 128Mi`; default limit `cpu: 200m`, `memory: 256Mi`; max `cpu: 500m`, `memory: 512Mi`
- a ResourceQuota with the `hard` keys `cpu: 2`, `memory: 2Gi`, `pods: 5`
- a Deployment `test-limits` with `2` replicas of `nginx` and **no** resources set, so the LimitRange defaults apply

Both Pods of `test-limits` must be Running.

verification.description: LimitRange exists with correct specifications
ResourceQuota exists with correct specifications
Deployment respects resource constraints

questions.question:
In the namespace `cluster-admin`, create the ServiceAccount `app-admin`, a Role `app-admin` and a RoleBinding `app-admin` so that the ServiceAccount can only:

- `get`, `list`, `watch` `pods` and `deployments`
- `update` `deployments`
- `create` and `delete` `configmaps`

It must not be able to create Pods. Then run a Pod `admin-pod` (image `bitnami/kubectl:latest`, command `sleep 3600`) as `app-admin`, with its token mounted (do not disable automounting).

verification.description: ServiceAccount exists with correct configuration
Role and RoleBinding are configured correctly
Test pod is running with correct ServiceAccount

questions.question:
In the namespace `network`, create the Deployments `web` (image `nginx`, label `app=web`), `api` (image `nginx`, label `app=api`) and `db` (image `postgres`, label `app=db`, env `POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust`). Then create two egress NetworkPolicies:

- `web-policy`: Pods `app=web` may only send traffic to Pods `app=api`
- `api-policy`: Pods `app=api` may only send traffic to Pods `app=db`

You may also allow DNS on port 53.

verification.description: Deployments exist with correct labels
Network policies exist with correct specifications

questions.question: In the namespace `upgrade`, create a Deployment `app-v1` (label `app=app-v1`, `4` replicas, image `nginx:1.19`, strategy `RollingUpdate` with `maxUnavailable: 1` and `maxSurge: 1`). Update it to `nginx:1.20`, record the change in the `kubernetes.io/change-cause` annotation, save the output of `kubectl rollout history deployment app-v1 -n upgrade` to `/tmp/exam/rollout-history.txt`, then roll back to `nginx:1.19`. At the end, all 4 Pods must be Ready and run `nginx:1.19`.

verification.description: Initial deployment exists with correct specifications
Rolling update performed correctly and history saved
Rollback completed successfully

In the namespace `scheduling`, run the Pods `high-priority` and `low-priority` (image `nginx`) using these classes, each with a **required** pod anti-affinity rule (`topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname`) against the other, so they always land on different nodes.
